To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the end region convective thermal resistance can be reduced significantly by using a combination of the following features: (i) a larger number of axial fans; (ii) a larger number and/or a larger size of axial fan blades; (iii) a smaller axial fan blade pitch; (iv) a smaller axial gap between the axial fan blade and the stator core; (v) a larger number or larger size of radial fans.

(1) the convective thermal resistance can be reduced by using a fan with a higher static pressure rise, (2) the convective resistance can be reduced with a lower air temperature, and (3) the convective heat transfer can be improved by using a fan that produces more turbulence in the air stream.

the cooling of the strip-wound totally enclose fan-cooled induction electric machine end region can be improved by: 1) using a fan with a larger diameter; 2) using a fan that has a larger number of blades and/or a larger chord length; and 3) using a fan whose blade angle is closer to the optimum value.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cooling of the stator end region of an electric machine.
the cooling of a two-polar, strip-wound totally-enclosed fan-cooled induction electric motor.
the cooling of the stator end region of a totally enclosed fan-coiled (TEFC) induction machine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a strip wound rotor, a larger fan, and an extended fan cover, all in combination with a reduced end-winding length, can lead to a reduction of the end region convective thermal resistance of about 50%.
the end region of strip-wound motors is a complex and difficult region in which to achieve low thermal resistance.
the end region of the TEFC induction machine can be cooled effectively by using the appropriate design and configuration of the end region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a single cooling fan in the end region is not effective, and that a double cooling fan arrangement should be used.
the end region of the totally enclosed fan-coiled induction machine can be cooled more effectively than is normally achieved by using a number of design features that have been identified.
the use of a fan with a larger diameter and a larger number of blades is beneficial.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not possible to cool the end region of an induction machine with an air gap of 2 mm by using the standard fan and duct configuration.
the end region cooling can be significantly improved by using a combination of features, including a large number of axial fans, an extended fan cover, and an extended end shield.
the end region of the machine is a critical region for the cooling performance.
